## Problem
`_run_plan_review` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, about line 625) runs `_apply_review_floors` only when `engine == "pipeline"`. Under the agentic engine, these steps are skipped:
- the Pass-3 rising floor;
- the completion floor;
- the drift floor (`drift_floor.maybe_apply`, which can downgrade BLOCK to PASS through `_recompute_verdict_after_drop`);
- the consistency cross-checks (`xcheck.maybe_apply_contradiction` and `maybe_apply_comment_trail`, which rewrite `verdict["blocking"]`);
- fix-unit grouping.

So for the same plan material and findings, the two engines can sign different verdict strings and blocking lists.

The code comment cites ADR 0123, but `docs/adr/0123-selectable-plan-review-engine.md` documents only the Layer-1 floor and claimability running first under both engines. It does not say that the post-dispatch tail is pipeline-only, or that the drift floor's convergence (a code-drift re-review of an unchanged plan converging back to PASS) does not apply to agentic reviews.

## Decision
The steps stay pipeline-only, and ADR 0123 is amended to say so and why (operator direction, 2026-11-13). No behavior change.

What `_run_plan_review` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`) runs only when `engine == "pipeline"`, checked at ca3768c970d:

Post-dispatch tail (`_apply_review_floors`):
- Rising floor and completion floor: drop surfaced **advisory** findings only; the completion floor is inert unless `verify.completion_floor_active`.
- Drift floor (`drift_floor.maybe_apply`): on a plan-unchanged, code-drifted re-review, drops a **novel** finding from the blocking or advisory list when its citations miss the drifted files, then re-derives the verdict string, so it can turn BLOCK into PASS.
- Cross-checks (`xcheck.maybe_apply_contradiction`, `maybe_apply_comment_trail`): drop contradicted or already-resolved findings from **both** lists and re-derive the verdict string; inert unless their `verify.*_xcheck_active` flags are on.
- Fix-unit grouping: one LLM sub-call that stamps co-cited blocking findings for the CLI; changes no bucket, count or verdict.

Pre-dispatch shortcuts (already commented in code as pipeline-only, but not in the ADR):
- Idempotent attestation reuse (`reuse.idempotent_reuse`), BLOCK verdict reuse (`reuse.verdict_reuse`) and progressive drift refresh (`orchestrator.drift_refresh`). Each reuses or re-signs a **pipeline** attestation or verdict, so under agentic each review runs the agent afresh.

Every tail step only removes or stamps findings; none adds a finding or turns PASS into BLOCK.

## Plan
1. Amend `docs/adr/0123-selectable-plan-review-engine.md` §6 ("Invariants both engines keep") with a bullet stating that the post-dispatch tail (5 steps) and the 3 pre-dispatch shortcuts run only under the pipeline engine, and why:
   - the operator decided on 2026-11-09 (§3) that an agentic verdict blocks only on `blocker` findings, with `major`, `minor` and `trivial` advisory. The drift floor and cross-checks remove findings from the blocking list, so running them on agentic verdicts would override that decision;
   - the rising and completion floors only thin advisory findings, and fix-unit grouping only stamps blocking findings for display; none changes an agentic verdict, and each is tuned to pipeline findings;
   - the 3 shortcuts reuse or re-sign a pipeline attestation or verdict, which an agentic review must not inherit;
   - each tail step only removes or stamps findings, so skipping them can keep a BLOCK the tail would have dropped from the same agentic findings, but cannot turn a BLOCK into a PASS. This is relative to running the tail on the same agentic findings, not to the pipeline's verdict; the engines produce different finding sets. It is consistent with the epic's no-bypass invariant, which the attestation binding (§5) enforces.
2. In the same bullet, state the consequence: ADR 0052 §2's re-review-stability contract (an unchanged, signed plan re-reviewed at a drifted HEAD yields no new blocking findings) is upheld by the drift floor, cross-checks and drift refresh, so it holds for the pipeline engine only. An agentic re-review after code drift runs the agent afresh and can surface new blocking findings.
3. Add a 2026-11-13 dated line to ADR 0123's amendment section recording this.
4. Add a dated 2026-11-13 note under `docs/adr/0052-plan-review-validation-consistency-and-re-review-stability.md` §2 saying the contract applies to the pipeline engine and pointing to ADR 0123 §6, so the contract's own home carries the scope.
5. `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Choosing an engine": add 1 sentence saying the pipeline's reuse, drift refresh, post-review floors and cross-checks, and so ADR 0052's re-review stability, apply to the pipeline engine only.
6. The ADR names the pinning test: `tests/unit/test_plan_review_agentic.py::test_post_dispatch_tail_runs_only_under_pipeline` asserts that `_apply_review_floors`, the single entry point for every tail step, runs for pipeline and never for an agentic review (floor-blocked, DET-passing and degraded). It pins the entry point, not each step; the ADR says so. Run that test.

No code, config key, env var or flag changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0123 §6 states that the post-dispatch tail (5 steps) and the 3 pre-dispatch shortcuts are pipeline-only, gives the reasons above, and states that ADR 0052 §2's re-review stability holds for the pipeline engine only; the amendment section carries a 2026-11-13 line.
- [ ] ADR 0052 §2 carries a dated 2026-11-13 note scoping the contract to the pipeline engine.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Choosing an engine" says the reuse, drift refresh, floors, cross-checks and ADR 0052 re-review stability are pipeline-only.
- [ ] The ADR names `test_post_dispatch_tail_runs_only_under_pipeline` as the test pinning the entry point, and that test passes.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
